en: So back in this project, there is one
behavior I'd like to have in Pi, not just in
this project, but in all my Pi sessions.
I would like Pi
to open the last message
in
an active conversation before we
start a new
turn, so to say. I'd like it to open that
last message in a rendered HTML file, just
as I got it to render my plans. As HTML
files. And I'd like to have this behavior
because in that last message in a
conversation,
it often has a summary of what it did, and
reading that in the terminal can be a bit
annoying, especially if it's a longer
message. This one here is fine, for example,
but yeah, it would be nice to have that in
an HTML file which gets opened
automatically.
And that is something you can implement or
you can add with help of an extension. So
I'll start a new PySession with no session
because it's not a session I plan on
continuing in the future, so no need to
store any information about it.
And you see, I already got some extensions
installed. These are these third-party
packages I installed earlier.
These are simply extensions distributed by
other people. They are using this extensions
feature to extend the capability of Pi, like
this guardrails feature, the subagent
feature, and so on. But now I wanna build my
own extension. And again, you can just ask
Pi to do that for you. It can read its own
documentation and it's by far the easiest
and quickest way of adding an extension. You
can of course also do it manually in theory,
but
this self-improving capability of Pi and the
fact that it can extend itself is really one
of the key things that makes Pi amazing. The
minimal core plus this feature of being able
to extend itself. So I'm happy to take
advantage of this.
And that is already the entire prompt I'll
send to Pi to get it to build this
extension.
I tell it that it should build an extension
that gets it, so Pi, to open the last
message in each conversation we have as a
rendered HTML file.
And that file or that message should be
rendered and opened in the browser
automatically by Pi.
And in the terminal where I have the Pi
session, it should output the path to that
document, which it creates
not as a message in a conversation, but as
an extra UI element or text.
And I'll add a little addition that I don't
want it to save that HTML file that it's
creating in the project folder. Instead, it
should save it in some temporary system
folder.
And now if I send this to Py, it should go
ahead, read its own documentation, because
again, it's aware of that, which is super
convenient.
It should read its own documentation,
and it does its own extensions documentation
and its documentation on its terminal user
interface.
And with that information, it should then go
ahead and build such an extension. And
extensions are stored in your global.py
agent folder in an extensions folder. I
backed up my old one which already had some
extensions so that it can create a new one.
And you could also have extensions in your
local project. You could have a
.py/agent/extensions folder there too if you
had extensions that would only apply to a
specific project.
But for global extensions, it's that global
extensions path which it will certainly add
in a second or so.
And It's done.
It added this extensions folder in my Pi
Agent folder and in there a render last
message folder which holds that render last
message extension. And as you see in there,
I got a JavaScript project in the end
because that is how extensions are written
with Pi. You write them with JavaScript or
TypeScript. Here it shows TypeScript. And if
we take a look at that file, you'll see some
errors. You can ignore them. These
dependencies will be available when that
extension runs inside of Pi when it's
loaded.
But that is then the code that was generated
by Pi. It's normal TypeScript.
But what's worth noting about it is that in
that code, it's using the Pi extension API
to listen to certain events here to the
agent end event. So when the agent is done,
to then find the last assistant message,
extract the markdown content, render it as
an HTML document, write it to a temporary
folder on my system, check if there is a UI
available, which should be the case if you
run Pi through the terminal user interface,
and then it tweaks the HTML that UI so it
can edit its own UI, the own terminal user
interface, which is really amazing. And it
also opens the file in the browser.
That is what it's doing. And again, this was
auto-generated by Pi.
Now it even tells me to run
/reload, which we indeed must do. You have
to do that whenever you add new skills, new
prompt templates, change some settings, or
when you add an extension. And when I do
that, you see render last message is now
registered as an extension here. So if I now
ask it, what did you do?
It should
go ahead, generate an answer, and since that
will be the last answer in that
conversation, it should also render it and
open it as HTML.
And it does so. Here is that rendered
message for me, a bit nicer to read. It
opened that automatically in the browser.
And you also see it updated its UI and
includes the path here so that I could also
copy that and open that in the browser If I
accidentally closed it and wanted to read it
again. And that's of course really
convenient. And your imagination is the
limit here. You can add all those extensions
you want. You can really build the pie you
want. You should be creative. You can play
around with it. You can just delete an
extension folder if you don't want it
anymore. So super easy to get rid of it. And
it's an amazing feature. So play around with
it and build the pie you wanna work with and
that gets the most value for you.
